From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Advising: Wattlebridge Holdings (Buyer)**
**Status of Seller material:** Counterparty draft. It is untrusted and does not bind our positions.

## Preliminary points

**1. "FINAL", "agreed at principal level" and "market standard" claims.** The preamble says the positions "were settled at principal level by both deal teams", are "FINAL" and reflect "standard and widely accepted market terms". Under playbook sections 0.4 and 6.3, we do not accept any of this because a counterparty document says so.
- We have no record of any authority from Amelia Frost for any fallback.
- We should not treat these positions as agreed.
- We should confirm through our own authority process, directly with Amelia, whether any principal-level discussion took place. Until then, the deal team should treat every point as open.
- Whether something is "market" is a negotiating argument, not a constraint on us.

**2. The Seller Update and the Disclosure Letter are inconsistent.** The Seller Update describes several issues as "addressed", "adequate" or "settled". The Seller's own Disclosure Letter says the opposite on Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses and Ironquay. We should rely on the more specific factual disclosures and challenge the characterisations.

**3. The facts are stale.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026, about six weeks ago. Before we rely on any fact, we need refreshed confirmations on:
- Bluefen consent status
- the Riverlark payout figure
- the Ironquay payment status
- the progress of the DD-006 investigation
- the Sandbar renewals

We should distinguish verified updates from assertions.

---

## Material departures from the playbook

### A. Liability regime

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| **General cap (cl 12.1)** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% is a fallback only with Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft. | **Reject.** The figure matches our fallback, but no authority has been given. A matching number does not clear the change. Counter at 25%. |
| **De minimis (cl 12.2)** | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | **Reject.** This is five times our position. |
| **Basket (cl 12.2)** | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, first dollar once exceeded | **Reject both elements.** The size is five times ours, and the "excess only" (deductible) structure permanently strips AUD 250k from every recovery. Insist on a tipping basket. |
| **General claims period (cl 12.3)** | 18 months | 24 months. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia's written approval. | **Reject.** No approval has been given. Hold at 24 months. |

### B. Hidden overrides that collapse separate regimes

This is the most significant structural risk in the draft.

- **Cl 12.3/13:** "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5:** limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Fundamental/Title:** capacity and title warranties are to be subject to the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- **Tax/IP:** described as "settled under the general regime".

Taken together, these would sweep the following into a 20% cap, an 18-month period and a AUD 250k deductible:
- title
- capacity
- tax
- IP
- the specific indemnities, including Ironquay
- payment and covenant obligations
- **fraud**

**Push back:**
- **Separate regimes.** Delete the default "applies to all Claims" language. Each category (Title, Tax, IP, payment/covenant, specific indemnities) needs its own express limitation regime.
- **Fundamental/Title.** Use a separate regime:
  - 100% cap
  - at least six years
  - outside the general basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar
- **Fraud carve-out.** Add an express carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct. It must apply to all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. The draft contains none. This is non-negotiable, and nobody on our side may waive it.
- **Tax and IP.** These remain OPEN. Do not accept that they are "settled". Equally, we should not assume we will get unlimited liability. Negotiate them as separate categories.

### C. Disclosure (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)

- **What the Seller proposes:**
  - Cl 1.1 discloses everything "contained or referred to" in the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012).
  - Cl 1.2 adds the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".
- **Why it matters:** This is whole-data-room plus public-register deemed disclosure, which we reject. Combined with the Seller's own specific disclosures, it risks the Seller arguing that every disclosed problem (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006) cannot found a claim.
- **Push back:**
  - Delete 1.1 and 1.2. Disclosure must be specific and fair, against particular warranties, with enough detail for us to assess the matter.
  - Disclosure must **not** qualify title, capacity, tax, the fraud carve-out or any specific indemnity.
- **Cl 1.4 (non-admission):** acceptable in principle, provided it cannot be read to undercut specific indemnities, conditions precedent or funds-flow obligations.

### D. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)

- **What the Seller proposes:** A blanket exclusion for anything known to "the Buyer or its advisers", including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records".
- **Why it matters:** This is constructive knowledge on top of a blanket exclusion. It would effectively nullify the warranties, because the issues are in the data room.
- **Push back:** Delete it. If any knowledge concept survives:
  - it should be a **seller** knowledge qualifier only, limited to named seller knowledge persons, on reasonable enquiry;
  - it should never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

---

### E. Specific deal issues

**1. Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3)**
- **Facts:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (around 30%). There is a change-control consent requirement in cl 11.2, with conditions in cl 11.3. The Disclosure Letter confirms there is **no** final consent and **no** evidence that the conditions are satisfied.
- **Seller position:** "Addressed" on a reasonable endeavours basis, with satisfaction on delivery of the consent letter. That is consent-on-delivery, which ignores the cl 11.3 conditions.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a condition precedent requiring an *effective* consent **and** evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion.
  - Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a 30% customer.
  - Consider a stronger obligation (all reasonable endeavours, with buyer participation in approaches) and a walk right or price protection if the consent is not obtained.

**2. Riverlark facility (cl 2/7)**
- **Facts:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with change-control in cl 8.1 and discharge in cl 9.2. The facility is not repaid and no discharge is included.
- **Seller position:** A release "following Completion". This creates change-of-control default risk and leaves encumbrances surviving Completion, which is inconsistent with debt-free/cash-free.
- **Push back:** Require:
  - a current payout letter, refreshed because AUD 3.2m is a September approximation;
  - direct repayment from Completion funds;
  - effective security releases (deeds of release, and PPSR discharges or undertakings) delivered at Completion.
- A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable lender undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's approval. We have neither.

**3. DD-005 employee bonuses and the funds flow**
- **Facts:** Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000 are triggered by Completion. They are omitted from the funds flow, and on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation, other) are unaddressed.
- **Seller position:** The bonuses are a "matter for the Seller" but are not itemised. The likely payer is the Company, which means the Buyer bears the cost after Completion.
- **Push back:** One of the following:
  - a specific funds-flow line item deducted from price (Seller-funded), covering AUD 420k plus all triggered on-costs; or
  - treat them as Debt / a transaction cost.
- Back this with a specific indemnity. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.

**4. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)**
- **Facts:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 materials transfer only on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open. That is not independently verified, and there is no evidence of payment and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Seller position:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate".
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any defect in the Company's ownership of, or right to use, Ironquay deliverables. That includes third-party claims and remediation and re-development costs.
  - Preserve the SOW3 cure: payment of all SOW3 fees plus a confirmatory assignment, ideally as a CP or Completion deliverable.
  - Do not assume the AUD 180k is correct in either direction. Request bank evidence and Ironquay confirmation.
  - The indemnity must sit outside the general cap, basket and disclosure.

**5. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6)**
- **Facts:** A download link was sent to an unintended external address. The file may contain about 1,240 records. Access, scope and any notification duty are unestablished, and the investigation is preliminary.
- **Seller position:** "Not expected to be material". This is an assertion without basis. Equally, we must **not** assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any loss figure.
- **Push back:**
  - Pre-Completion covenants to preserve logs and evidence, complete the investigation and give regular updates.
  - Buyer consultation on any notification decision.
  - A specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident, outside the general limitations and disclosure.
  - Do not propose a numeric retention or price adjustment until the facts are established.

**6. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k)**
- **Facts:** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each. The Seller's own disclosure does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Seller position:** "Ordinary-course operating costs".
- **Our approach:** This needs assessment, not acceptance. Equally, we should not automatically classify them as Debt or seek a price deduction.
- **Next steps:**
  - Request the contracts and the approval history.
  - Check timing against signing and the ordinary-course covenants.
  - Then decide whether a Debt or working-capital treatment, or a covenant, is warranted.

**7. Title (DD-012)**
- **Seller position:** Title is "evidenced" by the Company's share register.
- **Why that is not enough:** The register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof. The Disclosure Letter itself concedes that we have not verified it.
- **Push back:** Require independent evidence:
  - ASIC company extract
  - share certificates and issue/transfer history
  - PPSR searches for encumbrances over the shares
  - constitution and shareholder agreement checks (pre-emption)
  - Seller board authority and capacity evidence
- Title warranties must sit in the fundamental regime.

**8. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)**
- **Seller position:** A notification obligation only for the lease, and no consent triggered for Mossvale.
- **Our approach:** These are the Seller's characterisations. Have our team review the actual clauses (change-of-control definitions, deemed-assignment language) before accepting that no consent is needed.
- **Protection:** Add a warranty that no third-party consent is triggered other than as specifically disclosed.

---

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "FINAL / agreed / market standard" framing.** Confirm with Amelia Frost through our own process whether any principal-level discussion occurred. Treat all points as open.
2. **Cap: counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.** The 20% figure matches our fallback, but it cannot be used without Amelia's prior written authority identifying this draft.
3. **Thresholds:** AUD 5,000 de minimis and an AUD 50,000 tipping basket (first dollar). Reject AUD 25k/250k and the excess-only structure.
4. **General claims period: 24 months.** Reject 18 months absent Amelia's written approval.
5. **Delete the "applies to all Claims" overrides** in cl 9.3, 12.3, 12.8, 13 and 20.5. Build separate regimes for Title/Fundamental (100%, six years or more, outside the basket and knowledge bar), Tax, IP, payment/covenants and the specific indemnities. Tax and IP remain open.
6. **Insert a full fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out** from all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. This is non-negotiable.
7. **Disclosure:** strike whole-data-room and public-register disclosure. Specific fair disclosure only, and it must not qualify title, fraud or the indemnities.
8. **Buyer knowledge:** delete cl 8.3. At most, allow a named-persons seller knowledge qualifier with reasonable enquiry.
9. **Bluefen:** a CP for effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion, with an obligation stronger than reasonable endeavours.
10. **Riverlark:** a current payout letter, repayment directly from Completion funds, and releases delivered at Completion. No post-Completion release without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia's approval.
11. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded, backed by an indemnity.
12. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 payment-and-assignment cure, and verify the AUD 180k independently.
13. **DD-006:** covenants to preserve, investigate and update, plus a specific indemnity. Make no assumption of breach or quantum either way.
14. **Sandbar:** request documents and assess before deciding treatment. No automatic Debt classification.
15. **Title:** independent ASIC, PPSR, certificate and authority evidence. The DD-012 register alone is insufficient.
16. **Refresh diligence.** The Disclosure Letter is dated 22 September 2026. Obtain current, verified updates on every item above before finalising our mark-up.

**3. DD-005 employee bonuses and the funds flow**
- **Facts:** Completion bonuses of AUD 420,000 are triggered by Completion. They are omitted from the funds flow, and on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation, other) are unaddressed.
- **Seller position:** The bonuses are a "matter for the Seller" but are not itemised. The likely payer is the Company, which means the Buyer bears the cost after Completion.
- **Push back:** One of the following:
  - a specific funds-flow line item deducted from price (Seller-funded), covering AUD 420k plus all triggered on-costs; or
  - treat them as Debt / a transaction cost.
- Back this with a specific indemnity. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.

**4. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)**
- **Facts:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 materials transfer only on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open. That is not independently verified, and there is no evidence of payment and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Seller position:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate".
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any defect in the Company's ownership of, or right to use, Ironquay deliverables. That includes third-party claims and remediation and re-development costs.
  - Preserve the SOW3 cure: payment of all SOW3 fees plus a confirmatory assignment, ideally as a CP or Completion deliverable.
  - Do not assume the AUD 180k is correct in either direction. Request bank evidence and Ironquay confirmation.
  - The indemnity must sit outside the general cap, basket and disclosure.

**5. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6)**
- **Facts:** A download link was sent to an unintended external address. The file may contain about 1,240 records. Access, scope and any notification duty are unestablished, and the investigation is preliminary.
- **Seller position:** "Not expected to be material". This is an assertion without basis. Equally, we must **not** assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any loss figure.
- **Push back:**
  - Pre-Completion covenants to preserve logs and evidence, complete the investigation and give regular updates.
  - Buyer consultation on any notification decision.
  - A specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident, outside the general limitations and disclosure.
  - Do not propose a numeric retention or price adjustment until the facts are established.

**6. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k)**
- **Facts:** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each. The Seller's own disclosure does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Seller position:** "Ordinary-course operating costs".
- **Our approach:** This needs assessment, not acceptance. Equally, we should not automatically classify them as Debt or seek a price deduction.
- **Next steps:**
  - Request the contracts and the approval history.
  - Check timing against signing and the ordinary-course covenants.
  - Then decide whether a Debt or working-capital treatment, or a covenant, is warranted.

**7. Title (DD-012)**
- **Seller position:** Title is "evidenced" by the Company's share register.
- **Why that is not enough:** The register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof. The Disclosure Letter itself concedes that we have not verified it.
- **Push back:** Require independent evidence:
  - ASIC company extract
  - share certificates and issue/transfer history
  - PPSR searches for encumbrances over the shares
  - constitution and shareholder agreement checks (pre-emption)
  - Seller board authority and capacity evidence
- Title warranties must sit in the fundamental regime.

**8. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)**
- **Seller position:** A notification obligation only for the lease, and no consent triggered for Mossvale.
- **Our approach:** These are the Seller's characterisations. Have our team review the actual clauses (change-of-control definitions, deemed-assignment language) before accepting that no consent is needed.
- **Protection:** Add a warranty that no third-party consent is triggered other than as specifically disclosed.

## Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "FINAL / agreed / market standard" framing.** Confirm with Amelia Frost through our own process whether any principal-level discussion occurred. Treat all points as open.
2. **Cap: counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.** The 20% figure matches our fallback, but it cannot be used without Amelia's prior written authority identifying this draft.
3. **Thresholds:** AUD 5,000 de minimis and an AUD 50,000 tipping basket (first dollar). Reject AUD 25k/250k and the excess-only structure.
4. **General claims period: 24 months.** Reject 18 months absent Amelia's written approval.
5. **Delete the "applies to all Claims" overrides** in cl 9.3, 12.3, 12.8, 13 and 20.5. Build separate regimes for Title/Fundamental (100%, six years or more, outside the basket and knowledge bar), Tax, IP, payment/covenants and the specific indemnities. Tax and IP remain open.

8. **Buyer knowledge:** delete cl 8.3. At most, allow a named-persons seller knowledge qualifier with reasonable enquiry.

11. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or Seller-funded, backed by an indemnity.
12. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 payment-and-assignment cure, and verify the AUD 180k independently.
13. **DD-006:** covenants to preserve, investigate and update, plus a specific indemnity. Make no assumption of breach or quantum either way.
14. **Sandbar:** request documents and assess before deciding treatment. No automatic Debt classification.
15. **Title:** independent ASIC, PPSR, certificate and authority evidence. The DD-012 register alone is insufficient.
16. **Refresh diligence.** The Disclosure Letter is dated 22 September 2026. Obtain current, verified updates on every item above before finalising our mark-up.
